name: Bianca Trent
life: “I still remember two alphabets on the door of our old flat.” People around the public road outside the Port of Asphalt know Bianca by a small Wednesday habit. Bianca can recognize shift change by the lull between two groups of walkers.
voice: I offered my grandmother's spare number tile. Now there are two grandparents' handwritings over our front door.
appearance: Bianca has a deep crease beside the mouth when smiling. Look for a smooth side part with one rebellious curl. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a striped cotton shirt with one loose pocket corner secured with green thread. In conversation Bianca gathers both sleeves neatly before settling in.
personality: Bianca keeps other people's confidences so well that friends sometimes mistake discretion for taking sides. Bianca wants to be trusted and resents being asked for proof of it.
agenda: To mount the two handwritings above the family door.
family: Sasha Baldwin is Bianca’s cousin. Bianca remembers the birthdays. Sasha asks what the birthday guest would like this year. A present that was perfect at sixteen may be completely wrong at forty. They take the trouble of finding out. Asked about *A doctor moves away*, Sasha says, “I clean her office. She always notices the first orange I bring from my tree and nobody else at work does.”
connections: Valentina Carey. Both families keep their old numbering on the door and in the album.

reactions.situation: A resident asks for the old metal number back
reactions.response: Bianca asks who has already taken the metal down and where it was left.

reactions.situation: A colleague says somebody used the wrong name in public
reactions.response: Bianca asks which name they want to hear next time and uses it in the next ordinary introduction.

reactions.situation: When somebody asks who said it first
reactions.response: Bianca offers to introduce them to the person willing to put a name to it.
